Implement advance_commit(current_term, log_terms, match_indexes, commit_index) for an offline fixed-membership Raft leader audit. All four arguments are required. current_term is a built-in integer >=1; log_terms is a list of 0..64 positive integer entry terms in nondecreasing order, each <=current_term, with list position i-1 representing index i. match_indexes is a nonempty list of 1..31 built-in nonnegative integers, one per distinct fixed member, each <=len(log_terms); element0 is the leader and equals len(log_terms). commit_index is a built-in integer in 0..len(log_terms). Booleans are not integers here. These are stipulated valid durable same-term replication reports in a static crash-fault model, with no snapshots, joint membership or Byzantine behavior; do not implement the rest of Raft.

Only an index n>commit_index whose entry term equals current_term and which at least floor(N/2)+1 distinct members report matching through may advance the leader's direct counting rule. Return a built-in dictionary with exactly: new_commit (largest such index, or the old commit_index); newly_committed (a list of every index from old commit_index+1 through new_commit); eligible_current_term (the ascending list of all directly eligible current-term indexes strictly above old commit_index). Committing a current-term anchor includes its earlier prefix; an older-term majority alone cannot advance the direct rule, and an already-known commit index never regresses.

Return only built-in dictionaries/lists/integers. Every mutable returned container must be fresh and independent within and across calls and from inputs. Do not mutate any input or earlier returned object. Empty logs, a one-member group, no advancement and repeated calls are supported. Raise ValueError for malformed types or any listed domain violation, including an incorrect leader match index; do not perform I/O, use globals carrying state, or access a network. Use only the Python standard library.

Implement choose_proposal(members, ballot, preferred, reports), a pure offline phase-one value selector for the corrected basic single-decree Paxos profile. All arguments are required. members is a nonempty list of 1..15 distinct nonempty built-in strings, each at most32 characters. ballot is a built-in positive integer, and preferred is a nonempty built-in string at most32 characters. reports is a list of at most128 records, each a built-in dictionary with exactly acceptor, prepare_ballot, accepted. acceptor must name a member; prepare_ballot is a positive built-in integer. accepted is None or a dictionary with exactly ballot and value: its positive integer ballot is less than that report's prepare_ballot, and value is a nonempty string at most32 characters. Booleans are not integers. The fixed crash-fault instance uses globally unique ballots and one value per ballot. No network, acceptor mutation, membership changes or Byzantine handling is requested.

Ignore reports for a prepare_ballot different from the requested ballot when deciding readiness and value. Matching reports count distinct acceptor identities, so identical retransmitted matching records count once. Contradictory matching records for one acceptor, or matching accepted reports assigning different values to the same accepted ballot, are malformed and raise ValueError. Use all distinct matching reports as the prepare set. A majority requires floor(len(members)/2)+1 identities. Return exactly {"ready":bool,"responders":list[str],"source_ballot":int|None,"value":str|None}, with responders sorted by identifier. Before a majority, source_ballot and value are None. With a majority and all accepted reports empty, choose preferred and source_ballot=None. Otherwise choose the value from the largest ACCEPTED BALLOT in the matching prepare set and report that ballot; value frequency and arrival order do not decide.

Reject any other malformed schema, type or listed constraint with ValueError. Every mutable output container must be independent within/across calls and from all inputs; leave inputs and all earlier outputs unchanged. Support one member, duplicate identical replies, empty reports and repeated calls. Use only the standard library, no I/O, network or stateful globals.

Implement annotate_trace(n, trace, pairs) for an offline fully instrumented Lamport/full-vector clock trace. All arguments are required. n is a built-in integer1..8. trace is a list of0..64 event dictionaries with unique nonempty string id values (at most32 characters), a built-in integer process in0..n-1, and kind equal to local, send or receive. A local record has exactly id,process,kind. A send record additionally has message (a nonempty string at most32 characters, unique among sends) and to (a process integer0..n-1); these are its exact fields. A receive record additionally has message and no to field, and must name an earlier send to that receiver process. Self-send and repeated deliveries of a previously sent message are allowed; sends never received are also allowed. List order supplies a valid interleaving, but supplies NO causal edge between different processes by itself. pairs is a list of0..128 two-element string lists naming existing event IDs, with repeated and self-pairs allowed. Booleans are not integers.

All process scalar counters and n-component vectors start at zero. Each local/send event increments that process's scalar counter and own vector component once before labeling. A send attaches that actual full vector and scalar as an immutable snapshot. A receive sets scalar=max(local,send_scalar)+1, merges each vector component with the sent snapshot by maximum, then increments its own component once. Counters never reset, truncate or wrap. Modeled happened-before is the transitive closure of same-process event order and matching send-to-receive edges; message loss adds no receive edge.

Return exactly {"events":list,"orders":list}. events follows trace order; each entry is exactly {"id":str,"lamport":int,"vector":list[int]} with a full length-n vector. orders has one string per pair: same for identical event IDs, before when the left event happens before the right, after for the converse, and concurrent when neither holds. Full-vector strict order is componentwise<= with at least one<, not all components<, scalar order or a sum. Every returned mutable container must be fresh and independent within/across calls and from inputs; do not mutate inputs or any earlier output.

Raise ValueError for malformed schemas/types, duplicate event/send IDs, early or unmatched receives, wrong destinations, unknown pair IDs or any listed domain violation. Support empty traces/pairs, one process and repeated calls. Only standard-library Python; no I/O, network or stateful globals.

Implement run_fences(resources, events), a pure offline resource-side fencing simulation. All arguments are required. resources is a built-in dictionary of0..8 nonempty string resource IDs (at most32 characters), each mapped to exactly {"issued":int,"floor":int,"value":int}. issued>=0 is a durable issuer counter; floor is the durable epoch already installed at THAT resource, with0<=floor<=issued. value is an arbitrary integer. Booleans are not integers. events is a list of0..64 exact dictionaries: {"kind":"issue","resource":r}; {"kind":"install","resource":r,"token":t}; {"kind":"write","resource":r,"token":t,"delta":d}; or {"kind":"crash"}. Every r names an initial resource, d is an integer, and each supplied token is an integer1<=t<=that resource's current issued counter at that event. Tokens are stipulated authentic and authorized for that named resource/mode; there is no additional lease or authorization test in this model. Different resources have independent token namespaces.

issue increments issued and returns the new token but DOES NOT change the resource's floor. install accepts iff token>=floor, raising floor to max(floor,token) without changing value; a lower token is rejected. write atomically applies the same token>=floor gate, updating floor and adding delta to value if accepted, or changing nothing if rejected. Distinct writes in one epoch may use equal tokens and all execute; these tokens are not deduplication keys. crash preserves issued,floor,value at every resource. No state resets or wraparound occur.

Return exactly {"results":list,"states":list,"final":dict}. Each result is exactly {"kind":str,"resource":str|None,"token":int|None,"accepted":bool|None,"value":int|None}: issue gives its minted token, accepted=None and current value; install/write give the supplied token, their acceptance Boolean and resulting current value; crash uses None for the latter four fields. states contains a full resources-shaped snapshot after every event; final is a separate full snapshot after all events (a copy of initial state for an empty event list). Every mutable container must be independent within and across all results/snapshots/final/calls and from inputs, with no input or earlier-output mutation.

Malformed types/schemas, unknown resources, invalid initial bounds or invalid tokens raise ValueError. Support empty resource/event sets, one resource, lower/equal/higher tokens and repeated calls. Standard library only; no I/O, network or stateful globals.

Implement run_invocations(initial, events), a pure offline counter with atomic retained invocation deduplication. Both arguments are required. initial is any built-in integer, not a Boolean. events is a list of0..64 exact dictionaries: {"kind":"request","client":c,"request":i,"delta":d}; {"kind":"forget","client":c,"request":i}; or {"kind":"crash"}. c is a nonempty built-in string of at most32 characters encoding the client's incarnation/namespace; i is a built-in nonnegative integer request identifier, and d is an integer payload. The full identity is (client,request), and canonical payload equality here is exact delta equality. All requests are otherwise authorized and the protected counter is the entire local effect boundary; there are no external effects.

Start with total=initial and an empty durable ledger. A request atomically rechecks the ledger at its effect commit: a new key adds delta to total, stores the exact delta and ORIGINAL resulting total as reply, and returns status executed; a retained key with the same delta returns status replayed and its original stored reply without changing anything; a retained key with a different delta returns status conflict, reply=None and no mutation. Later unrelated requests may change total; a matching retry must still return its original reply. forget explicitly ends retention for the named key, removing its record but not undoing its effect, returning status forgotten if present or absent otherwise and reply=None. A later retry after that removal has no other duplicate evidence and is treated as a new commit. crash preserves total and ledger, returning status recovered and reply=None.

Return exactly {"results":list,"snapshots":list,"final":dict}. Each result has exactly kind,status,reply. Every snapshot after an event, and the separate final snapshot, has exactly {"total":int,"ledger":list}; ledger entries are exactly {"client":str,"request":int,"delta":int,"reply":int}, sorted lexicographically by(client,request). With no events, results/snapshots are empty and final has the initial total and empty ledger. Every mutable output container must be fresh and independent within/across outputs, snapshots, final and calls and from inputs. Do not mutate inputs or any previous output.

Raise ValueError for malformed schemas/types, empty/oversized client names, negative request IDs or any listed violation; booleans are not integers. Support empty events, repeated calls, interleaved different identities, conflicts, retained retries, explicit eviction and crash. Only standard-library Python, no I/O, network or stateful globals.
